tracks.legalName: Automatic sealing, non-convictions and 10-year misdemeanor convictions, D.C. Code § 16-805
tracks.publicName: Automatic sealing, non-convictions and 10-year misdemeanor convictions

citations: D.C. Code § 16-805, as amended by D.C. Law 25-175 and D.C. Law 26-52
controllingAuthority.summary: Mandatory on the Court, no motion, no prosecutor or victim objection step. Non-convictions sealed by October 1, 2027 or within 90 days after termination or final disposition, whichever is later; qualifying misdemeanor convictions by October 1, 2027 or within 90 days after the waiting period expires, whichever is later.

eligibleDispositions: citations, arrests, or charges where the case was terminated by the prosecutor or reached a final disposition and did not result in a conviction or an insanity acquittal under § 24-501
misdemeanor convictions where at least 10 years have elapsed since completion of the sentence
exclusions: § 16-805(b), 17 categories: intrafamily offense (§ 16-1001(8)); parental kidnapping (§ 16-1022); criminal abuse of a vulnerable adult or elderly person (§ 22-933); financial exploitation of a vulnerable adult or elderly person (§ 22-933.01); refusal or neglect of a guardian to provide for a child under 14 (§ 22-1102); incest (§ 22-1901); misdemeanor sexual abuse (§ 22-3006); Chapter 30A of Title 22 (non-consensual pornography); Chapter 31 (sexual performance using minors); Chapter 31A (stalking); an offense requiring sex offender registration under Chapter 40 where the registration period has not expired; violation of Chapter 40 as described in § 22-4015; a dangerous crime under § 23-1331(3); a crime of violence under § 23-1331(4); DUI (§ 50-2206.11); commercial vehicle DUI (§ 50-2206.12); and operating while impaired (§ 50-2206.14).

waitingPeriods.duration: 10 years since completion of the sentence

tracks.legalName: Motion to Seal a Non-Conviction Record, D.C. Code § 16-806(a)(1)

citations: D.C. Code § 16-806(a)(1), as amended by D.C. Law 24-284 (applicable March 1, 2025), D.C. Law 26-52 (October 28, 2025), and D.C. Law 26-81 (temporary, January 29, 2026)
controllingAuthority.summary: The Court shall grant if sealing is in the interests of justice, § 16-806(b)(1), weighing the movant's interest, the community's interest in rehabilitation and reintegration, and the community's interest in retaining access. The published section carries amendments by temporary legislation that expire September 11, 2026.

eligibleDispositions: case terminated by the prosecutor or reached final disposition, no conviction and no § 24-501 insanity acquittal
exclusions: If the offense is not on the § 16-805(b) list, the motion must be filed before October 1, 2027. If the offense is on that list, there is no deadline.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Seal a Conviction Record, D.C. Code § 16-806(a)(3)

controllingAuthority.summary: Conviction sealing once the waiting period has run, on the interests-of-justice standard. A felony in Offense Severity Group 1, 2, or 3 of the Sentencing Commission Master Grid as of March 10, 2023 is not eligible.

eligibleDispositions: conviction, with the waiting period run
exclusions: A felony in Offense Severity Group 1, 2, or 3 of the Sentencing Commission Master Grid as of March 10, 2023 is not eligible.

The § 16-805(b) exclusion list applies to automatic sealing, not to motion sealing of convictions. A DUI conviction, an intrafamily offense conviction, and the other categories remain eligible for motion sealing once the waiting period runs.

waitingPeriods.duration: 5 years from completion of the sentence
8 years from completion of the sentence

geography.venue: District of Columbia Superior Court, Criminal Division; one motion per case number in the case being addressed.

destination.name: Superior Court of the District of Columbia, Criminal Division
destination.detail: Court-controlled, with a clerk intake step through the Criminal Division Seal Team. The conviction waiting periods may be waived by the prosecutor in writing, § 16-806(e).

components.notes: No official form exists. The statute fixes the content of the motion.

participantInputs.question: What is the case number, and what were you convicted of?
Was the conviction a misdemeanor or a felony, and what was the statute section?
On what date did you complete the sentence — the latest of discharge from incarceration, commitment, probation, parole or supervised release?
List every citation, arrest, charge and conviction of yours that has not already been sealed or expunged, as far as you know them.
In your own words, why is sealing this record in the interests of justice — what does it stop you doing now?
Which of your records do you want sealed? You do not have to ask for all of them.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Set Aside a Conviction under the Youth Rehabilitation Act, D.C. Code § 24-906(e-1)

controllingAuthority.summary: A youth offender, meaning a person who was 24 or younger at the time of the offense, may move to set aside the conviction after completing probation, incarceration, supervised release, or parole, whichever is later, regardless of whether they were sentenced under the YRA. Discretionary: the court considers the § 24-903(c)(2) factors and makes a written statement on the record of its reasons.

eligibleDispositions: a conviction for an offense committed when the person was 24 or younger, after completing probation, incarceration, supervised release, or parole, whichever is later

waitingPeriods.condition: Completion of probation, incarceration, supervised release, or parole
waitingPeriods.duration: Whichever is later; no further period stated
